static_review: Default mode verifies without object writes. Explicit --write is reachable only after requested SHA matches API and a unique reconstructed commit hashes exactly.
Independent Python Git-object hash is checked again by git hash-object; direct tree and parent object types must exist, original parent order is preserved.
Optional write uses git hash-object -w -t commit --stdin and verifies raw object bytes; no update-ref, checkout, merge, push or network commands exist.
Git invocation is an argument list, strips inherited GIT_* settings, disables replacement objects and hooks, and limits individual commands to 30 seconds.
Signed payload and signature folding are preserved; the helper reports API verification but makes no independent PGP trust claim.
JSON input is capped at 2 MiB, duplicate members reject, parent/header/candidate reconstruction counts are finite; evidence outputs use exclusive creation.
limitations: Review covers this exact helper byte set and exact commit-object reconstruction. Repository reference updates remain separate actions.
Author evidence reports seven tests including object write/readback in a disposable bare repository; reviewer reran only six pure reconstruction controls with real subprocess creation forbidden.
